title: Geo Data Residency Exception - Evidence & Negotiation Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose
This is a working playbook for evaluating, documenting, and negotiating customer requests for geo-specific data residency exceptions (requests that data, telemetry, logs, or model artifacts be stored or never leave a particular country/region). It is intended for use by sales, solutions engineering, and legal to: 1) decide when an exception is acceptable, 2) collect required evidence, and 3) provide minimal contractual language and operational mitigations.

Scope and assumptions
- Applies to hosted and dedicated modalities where customers request: specific residency for raw prompt data, ephemeral KV cache persistence, logs/observability telemetry, or backups.
- Does NOT replace full DPA negotiation. Treat as a fast-track alignment doc for low-to-medium-risk customers and as a checklist for handing high-risk cases to Legal & Privacy.
- Assumes control-plane remains in Redwood unless customer explicitly requests control-plane colocation.

Quick decision rubric (one-pager)
1) Customer tier: enterprise with regulated data (finance, healthcare, public-sector)? If yes -> escalate to Legal + Privacy + Sales Engineering.
2) Data type: PHI/PCI/hash of identifiers? If yes -> default deny without Private deployment or on-prem (unless Contract + SOC2 evidence accepted).
3) Retention ask: persistent storage vs ephemeral cache only? If ephemeral only, we can often comply with policy + technical controls.
4) Evidence required: onshore proof-of-storage + encryption key custodian statement + KMS audit logs.

Evidence & artifacts checklist (minimum set to accept exception)
- Written request from customer specifying exact scope (buckets, log streams, telemetry types).
- Architecture sketch showing data flows with ingress/egress points.
- Proof of storage location(s): cloud provider region+bucket names or private colo rack IDs.
- KMS integration evidence: key policy with geographic scope, key identifiers, and rotation schedule.
- Retention & deletion mechanism description and test plan.
- Audit/monitoring plan: who/what will log access and how often evidence will be produced.
- Legal attestation: statement of non-replication to other regions and fallback behavior (e.g., encrypted backup to cold storage in another region only if requested and with notice).
- If asking for no outbound telemetry: list of telemetry IDs removed or obfuscated and sample sanitized logs.

Acceptable evidence formats (examples)
- Cloud provider export: S3 bucket metadata, object location tags, region tag, or provider access logs.
- KMS logs: key usage events showing key material used in-region.
- Internal runbook excerpts and screenshots showing routing tables and firewall rules.
- Signed letter from engineering lead + solutions architect certifying the deployment topology (template below).

Template: Engineering attestation (one paragraph)
"We confirm that all customer-specified data types (prompts, response logs, embeddings) for Customer X are stored exclusively within the [cloud region name / colo identifier] under account [account id]. Keys used to encrypt these objects are managed via [KMS provider] with key IDs [ids] and are configured to restrict export outside [region]. Backups are disabled / configured as follows: [backup policy]. Access to storage is limited to roles: [list]. This attestation is provided on behalf of Redwood Inference by [engineer name], [title], on [date]."

Suggested minimal contract language (negotiation starting point)
- Residency scope: "Provider will store and process Customer Data solely in the geographic region(s) identified in Exhibit A, unless Customer provides prior written consent."
- Audit and evidence delivery: "Provider will provide engineering attestation and supporting logs on a quarterly basis or upon Customer's reasonable request (subject to standard redaction and availability windows)."
- Fallback & incident clause: "If Provider must restore data from backup in a different region due to catastrophic failure, Provider will notify Customer within 24 hours and provide proof of deletion of the restored copy after remediation."
- Limitation & exception: "Customer acknowledges that control-plane operations and aggregated telemetry (anonymized for platform health) may be processed outside the region, as described in Exhibit B."

Negotiation play tips for Sales + Legal (notes to self)
- Start with: what exact artifacts do they need to prove residency? Ask for acceptance of engineering attestation first (cheaper) before contract exhibits.
- If customer insists on contractual exhibit, keep language narrow (named buckets, specific log types, time-bounded clause). Avoid blanket geographic guarantees across unknown future features.
- Offer mitigations instead of flat denials: tighter role-based access, additional encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key), audit window SLAs.
- Have a fall-through: Private deployment or on-prem checklist if negotiation stalls.

Common negotiation red flags (require immediate legal escalation)
- Customer requires liability shift for noncompliance with their local law (they want Provider to bear regulatory fines).
- Requests for permanent deletion attestations without technical auditability.
- Demands for control-plane colocation without clear SOW & commercial terms.

Operational controls we can offer (technical mitigations)
- Customer-managed KMS keys (BYOK) with key material kept in-region.
- Region-locked buckets with VPC/Gateway endpoints to prevent accidental replication.
- Disable cross-region replication for specified buckets.
- Retention/auto-delete lifecycle policies with certificate of deletion runbooks.
- Tokenization/proxying layer that strips or hashes sensitive fields before they are stored in telemetry.

Escalation matrix (playbook flow)
1) Solutions Engineer collects initial request + fills Evidence checklist (this doc).
2) Sales legal counsel does a 72h pass: approve template clause or escalate.
3) If red flags present -> schedule a legal + privacy + infra sync within 4 business days.
4) For Private/on-prem asks -> hand to commercial engineering for SOW and cost estimate.

Open questions / decisions to resolve (internal)
- What is the standard evidence delivery SLA we can promise to customers? (30d, 14d, 7d?) Need input from Infra.
- Do we accept KMS snapshots as proof of in-region key usage or must we provide monthly signed attestations?
- Standard retention window for audit logs we will keep for customer evidence (default 90d) — confirm with Observability team.

Reference templates + links
- Minimal residency exhibit (draft) -> CONFLUENCE:Geo-Residency-Exhibit (link above).
- Sales checklist ticket: JIRA-SEC-4827 (attached).
- Related: cross-border segmentation annex (see policy library) — use as input but avoid copy/paste.

Notes for legal drafter (short)
- Keep clause scoped to "Customer Data" as defined in DPA; avoid broader platform-level guarantees.
- Insert explicit exclusions for aggregated telemetry and third-party monitoring tools.
- Add a short remediation timeline for cross-region restoration and deletion verification.

Appendix: sample email to request evidence from infra (copyable)
Subject: Request: Residency evidence for Customer X (ticket JIRA-SEC-4827)
Hi infra team,

Customer X requires proof that customer data (prompts + embeddings) are stored only in AWS eu-west-1. Please provide:
1) S3 bucket names and region tags.
2) KMS key IDs and policy notes restricting export.
3) Any replication/backup configurations (disabled/enabled).
4) A short attestation sentence we can use in contract exhibits.

Thanks — Leah (on behalf of Sales + Legal)

--
Draft status notes: this file is intended to be iterative. If you use the attestation or exhibit language for an active negotiation, copy the clause into the customer-specific doc and tag this doc with the JIRA/Confluence link for auditability.

Unresolved: consider adding a short checklist for telemetry obfuscation patterns (PII detection rules) — assigned to Observability (Priya).

End of draft.
